lead: >-
  Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia are brought together in an extensive journey across South America: walks beside the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, boat excursions in the Galapagos, and a visit to the El Peñón de Guatapé rock in Colombia. Discover which parts of the itinerary are genuinely active, which stage calls for special preparation, and why this route should not be mistaken for a standalone three-country tour.

## What adventures await in Argentina, Colombia and Ecuador

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The specific option is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Argentina features near the beginning, while Ecuador and Colombia appear toward the end. The itinerary also includes Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru between those stages. The three-country filter therefore shows **part of a much larger journey's geography**, not a direct Argentina–Ecuador–Colombia trip.

Adventure is a secondary theme of this tour. That distinction matters when setting expectations: the itinerary combines nature walks, boat journeys, city tours and more active stretches in other countries. It does not confirm dedicated trekking in each of these three countries, rafting or a volcano ascent.

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls and a walk beside the cascades

The Argentine stage starts in [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), with a [group excursion to the Argentine side of the falls](/argentina/puerto-iguazu/iguazu-argentina-group-russian-program/) accompanied by a Russian-speaking guide. Travellers then fly to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where the experience changes to a city tour followed by a tango show with dinner.

Visitors come to Iguazu for the waterfalls, humid forest and the sensation of standing close to rushing water. Non-slip shoes and protection for belongings against spray are useful. Nevertheless, a waterfall excursion should not automatically be treated as a sporting hike. The length of accessible walks and the exact sections used depend on the park's visiting conditions and that day's confirmed programme.

If your aim is a long-distance walking journey in Argentina, you will need a different product with appropriate trekking days, rather than expecting a demanding hike during a sightseeing visit to Iguazu.

## Ecuador: an island journey rather than mountain trekking

After Peru, the route reaches Quito and then the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), travellers explore the island highlands and lava tunnels. A separate day is devoted to a boat excursion: **either North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrion**. Which of these two alternatives takes place is confirmed at booking. Both cannot be promised.

A visit to [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) marks the transition from the mainland to an archipelago where landing conditions, sea swell and protected-area rules shape each day. Plan for sun protection, comfortable shoes for shore visits and waterproof protection for belongings. Scuba diving, equipment hire and encounters with specific animals are not automatically included in this programme.

Quito sits high in the Andes, while the island section takes place beside the ocean. One wardrobe will not suit both: lightweight coastal clothing needs to be paired with a warm layer for the mainland highlands. Any additional Galapagos documents and conservation fees should be checked separately before departure.

## Colombia: Guatapé, Medellín and the contrast of the Caribbean coast

After the Guayaquil–Medellín flight, the itinerary includes an excursion to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). This eight-hour day has an English-speaking guide, transfers between locations and views over the reservoir. **Climbing the staircase to the top of the rock must not be assumed to be included without confirmation**: the itinerary specifies a visit to the site, but the exact level of physical exertion needs to be agreed.

Next come [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) in Medellín, followed by Cartagena, Bogotá and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). These stops are primarily cultural and sightseeing experiences. Flying between cities and exploring on foot are different from an active mountain route.

| Stage | Actual format |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Guided visit to Iguazu, followed by Buenos Aires |
| Ecuador | Santa Cruz and one of two island itineraries |
| Colombia | Guatapé and a full programme of city excursions |

## Logistics and time to recover between active days

An extensive journey through other countries separates the Argentine and Ecuadorian stages. Before booking, compare the complete [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) with your travel goals. If the priority is several days in the Galapagos followed by Colombia, there is a separate [12-day Ecuador–Colombia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/). However, it **is not part of this three-country selection**, because it does not visit Argentina.

Allow for changes in climate zones, flight connections, Quito's altitude, island transport and recovery after intensive days. We help coordinate the travel sequence, identify where additional nights may be needed and discuss the precise conditions of individual activities in advance. Entry and transit requirements must be checked against each traveller's nationality and all countries actually visited, rather than just the three names in the filter.

For other options, see the [Argentina + Colombia + Ecuador selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador/). Our full range of multi-country [adventure itineraries](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) offers a broader choice of destinations and activity levels.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I travel only through Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia on this itinerary?

The published 32-day itinerary covers eight countries. Reducing it to three would require a separately designed route and confirmation of new flights and services; it would be a different trip.

### Is an ascent of El Peñón de Guatapé included?

A visit to the rock and its surroundings on the excursion day is confirmed. The climb itself and its conditions must be checked separately.

### Will we take both Galapagos island routes?

No. The programme offers a choice between North Seymour with Bachas Beach and South Plaza with Cape Carrion. Only one option takes place.

### Is the trip suitable for someone without trekking experience?

Most of the stages described here involve sightseeing. However, the full itinerary also includes high-altitude travel outside these three countries and active days. Discuss your capacity for the full journey and your health needs, rather than relying on the thematic label alone.

## A cultural route through Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia: what is included

For an introduction to the cultures of these three countries, our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The relevant itinerary is [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia, it passes through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. This is essential when planning: **travellers do not head straight from Argentina to Ecuador**, but continue through an extensive South American itinerary.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The cultural experiences in the selected countries are clearly differentiated. Argentina introduces the everyday life of Buenos Aires and tango. Ecuador reveals Quito's Spanish colonial heritage before shifting the focus to the natural world of the Galapagos. Colombia brings the journey to a close with Medellín's history and contemporary art, Caribbean Cartagena and Bogotá's museums.

## Argentina: a port city, its neighbourhoods and tango

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the programme includes a sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide and an evening tango performance with dinner. Exploring the city takes visitors through [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta and Puerto Madero. Each tells a different story within the same city: old harbour districts, civic squares and modern urban development.

Tango is the main cultural highlight of the Argentine stage. The performance is included on a specific day of the itinerary, so it is part of the programme rather than an incidental optional extra. Travellers explore the neighbourhoods by day and watch music and dance performed on stage in the evening.

Before Buenos Aires, the itinerary includes a visit to the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The waterfalls and national park walkways provide a break in nature before the city's cultural attractions, but are not themselves a historical excursion. For the wider combination of destinations, see our [Argentina, Colombia and Ecuador selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador/).

## Ecuador: historic Quito and a change of focus on the islands

In [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), an excursion through the historic city includes churches, squares and examples of colonial art. The route also visits the equator line, [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the Intiñan Museum. These attractions offer a different comparison with Buenos Aires: a mountain capital, colonial religious architecture and local traditions rather than port-city history and tango.

Quito is at considerable altitude, so a sensible walking pace is helpful after the flight from Lima. For an excursion day, it is more useful to confirm which churches and museums will actually be visited than to squeeze additional sights into limited time. Opening hours and access to individual buildings should be checked for the travel dates.

The journey then flies to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). This section is primarily about nature: Santa Cruz, the island highlands and a boat excursion. When choosing a **culture and history** trip, it is important not to present the Galapagos days as a continuation of Quito's museum programme. They broaden the experience of Ecuador but serve another interest.

## Colombia: from Medellín's urban transformation to colonial Cartagena

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary includes [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). This stop reveals a neighbourhood whose contemporary cultural life has become an important part of the Medellín experience. Another day includes El Peñol, the El Peñón rock and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), known for its colourfully painted house façades. The combination brings together urban history, contemporary art and architectural traditions.

The next contrast is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), a Caribbean port with a fortified historic centre. The excursion names San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, old streets, squares and the Church of San Pedro Claver. A full sightseeing day is devoted to Cartagena, allowing more time for its colonial history than a short transit stop would.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the itinerary turns to museums and art: the historic centre, Gold Museum, Botero collection and Monserrate. A subsequent excursion goes to the Salt Cathedrals in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). Museum hours and the final list of visits should be confirmed before departure, since a particular exhibition's closure can change the day's order.

## How to divide your time between history and travel

This itinerary has three cultural centres with different lengths of stay: Buenos Aires, Quito and several Colombian cities. Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru lie between the Argentine and Ecuadorian stages. The selected three countries are part of a 32-day journey, rather than an independent series of three or four direct connections.

Travellers interested primarily in museums, architecture and local customs have a practical choice. The complete itinerary provides a broad context: tango in Argentina, Inca heritage in Peru, Ecuadorian colonial art, and Colombia's Caribbean culture and contemporary urban life. A shorter trip visiting just the three countries can be discussed separately, but its excursions, flights and price cannot be assumed to match the published tour.

When arranging the journey, Ada Tours helps coordinate the order of countries, domestic flights and ground excursions. Documents, transit rules and entry requirements are checked for each traveller's nationality and every country on the route; there is no single entry permit for all of South America. Different currencies and payment rules also call for a separate spending plan, particularly on such a long journey.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel in Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia

### Can we visit only these three countries using the published itinerary?

The published [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) travels through eight countries. Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia are three major stages, with other countries in between. A shortened itinerary would require separate arrangements.

### Where does this combination include the most historical excursions?

In Argentina, the main cultural day is devoted to Buenos Aires and tango. In Ecuador, it focuses on historic Quito. Colombia's cultural programme is spread across Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

### Does the Galapagos visit count as part of the culture and history programme?

The Galapagos section primarily explores the islands' natural environment. It belongs to the same long tour, but Quito is far more important for history, art and architecture. To compare itineraries focused on wildlife and birdwatching, see [Argentina, Colombia and Ecuador: Wildlife and Safari](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador/interests/wildlife/). The tour in question includes wildlife watching in the Galapagos; including a country in a selection does not imply a safari in every one of its regions.

### Should museums and historic sites be booked in advance?

The excursions are set out in the itinerary, but access to individual museums, churches and exhibitions depends on the visiting date. During trip planning, opening times, possible closures and the order of excursions are checked before flight connections and the final daily schedule are confirmed.

## Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia: from Iguazu to the Galapagos Islands

There is no single short nature-focused itinerary linking these three countries: [Argentina](/argentina/) lies in the south of the continent, [Ecuador](/ecuador/) straddles the equator, and [Colombia](/colombia/) completes the northern part of this extensive journey. One tour nevertheless includes remarkably different natural attractions: **Iguazu Falls, the volcanic islands of the Galapagos archipelago, and mountain scenery in the Colombian Andes**.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. We offer a [32-day itinerary through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Besides these three, the trip passes through Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The order and duration of nature stops are determined by the complete itinerary, not by the sequence of country names in the themed catalogue.

## Iguazu in Argentina: water and Atlantic Forest

The Argentine section includes [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and a visit to the Argentine side of the falls. Travellers first see the waterfalls in Brazil and then enjoy views from the other side of the border. These two days let them experience the same natural complex from different visitor routes, but the visits take place in two different countries.

Iguazu National Park protects not only the cascades but also the surrounding subtropical forest. According to UNESCO, the waterfall system extends for almost three kilometres, and the humid environment around the falls supports a rich diversity of plants and wildlife. The main focus of the planned excursion is the waterfalls; encounters with particular wild animals cannot be guaranteed.

This is the most substantial nature-focused section of the Argentine stage. The itinerary then moves on to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for sightseeing, city neighbourhoods and tango. The entire Argentine part should not be described as a national-park trek, and Patagonia should not be added to expectations: it is not included in the published programme.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and the marine environment of the Galapagos

After the Andes and Peru, the journey reaches Ecuador. There is an initial stop in Quito and a visit to the equator-line area, followed by a flight to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Here the natural setting changes to volcanic islands, coastal scenery, the Santa Cruz highlands and the archipelago's distinctive ecosystems.

The itinerary includes [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and its highland area, with an island excursion the following day. One important choice must be preserved precisely: the programme specifies **North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrion**. These are alternatives for one day, not a promise to visit every location listed. The actual option depends on the confirmed arrangements.

UNESCO describes the Galapagos as an archipelago with a high proportion of endemic species, shaped by isolation and volcanic processes. Yet visiting the country does not in itself guarantee seeing every well-known Galapagos animal. Expectations should be based on the specific island excursion, weather conditions and permitted route.

## Colombia: Guatapé Rock and the mountain city of Bogotá

After Ecuador, the tour continues through Medellín, [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). These are Colombia's key natural highlights on this route: a towering rock formation, surrounding water and rolling hills. They offer a very different photographic setting and walking experience from Iguazu's cascades and the Galapagos' oceanic islands.

Colombia also features Cartagena and Bogotá, both with sightseeing days. [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) offers views of the terrain around the high-altitude capital, but is included as part of the city programme. No independent hike through a remote Colombian national park is advertised. That distinction matters for anyone seeking trekking or several days devoted to watching wild animals.

## What the one matching tour actually includes

| Country | Natural attraction and format |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Excursion to the Argentine side of Iguazu |
| Ecuador | Santa Cruz, the Galapagos and one of the alternative island programmes |
| Colombia | Guatapé, El Peñón Rock and views from Monserrate |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Of the three countries, Ecuador has the most extensive island-nature section, while Argentina's Iguazu is the most recognisable waterfall attraction. Colombia adds mountain views, although its itinerary is predominantly urban sightseeing. If you want more time in the national parks of each country, consider discussing a custom itinerary: the published journey is designed to introduce travellers to eight countries.

## Preparing for changes in natural environments

Iguazu is humid and hot, the mountains around Quito and Bogotá bring altitude and cooler temperatures, while the Galapagos are shaped by sea conditions and boat transfers. For one journey, pack lightweight clothes, a waterproof layer, comfortable footwear and protection for electronics against spray and seawater. Physical demands at Guatapé Rock and in the highlands should be agreed with the participants' needs in mind.

The countries between the three selected destinations are equally important. The itinerary includes flights and overland crossings through Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Visa and transit requirements are checked according to nationality for all eight countries; a themed selection is not a three-country travel ticket. The availability of island excursions also needs to be matched to confirmed transport and local regulations.

Currencies and payment methods vary: Argentina uses the peso, Colombia the Colombian peso and Ecuador the US dollar. Whether a particular bank card works depends on the issuing bank and payment infrastructure. Ada Tours helps coordinate logistics, excursions and the conditions of the extended programme. The unfiltered combination is available in the [Argentina–Colombia–Ecuador catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions about the nature of the three countries

### Can we see Iguazu and the Galapagos on one tour?

Yes. Both are included in the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), although several other countries and numerous excursions come between them.

### Do we visit all of North Seymour, Bachas, South Plaza and Cape Carrion?

No. The island day is described as an alternative: one combination of places **or** the other. The final option needs to be confirmed against the programme.

### Is a dedicated Colombian nature tour part of the route?

The Colombian stage features Guatapé, El Peñón and views around Bogotá. However, the published 32-day itinerary does not include a multi-day hike through national parks there.

### Where is the greatest contrast in natural scenery?

Iguazu reveals humid subtropical forest and a vast waterfall system, while the Galapagos offer volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean. These contrasting landscapes are a major reason to choose the journey for nature.

## Wildlife and safaris: where animal watching is planned on the route

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), visiting Argentina near the start and Ecuador and Colombia near the end. Other distinct stages lie between them. The three countries named in the filter share the **main geographical coverage of the itinerary**, while the theme of 'Wildlife and Safaris' applies to the tour as a whole because of the included animal-watching experiences in the Galapagos.

The distinction is important: the nature days in these three countries differ considerably. Argentina offers waterfalls and tropical forest; Ecuador brings island ecosystems and Galapagos excursions; Colombia offers landscapes around the Guatapé reservoir as part of a predominantly city-based sightseeing journey. There is no separate itinerary promising guaranteed wildlife watching in each of the three countries.

## Argentina: Iguazu, waterfalls and humid forest

In [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travellers visit the Argentine side of the falls on a [group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide](/argentina/puerto-iguazu/iguazu-argentina-group-russian-program/). The principal attractions on this day are the cascades, patches of forest and viewing trails within the national park.

For a nature-oriented journey, the appeal of Iguazu lies in the combination of waterfalls and surrounding vegetation. However, the day's itinerary does not include a dedicated specialist walk with an ornithologist and makes no promise of encounters with particular birds or mammals. If seeing specific species matters more than the waterfalls, discuss this before choosing the route.

After Iguazu, the tour continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). City sightseeing and tango with dinner are cultural experiences, so travellers should not expect the nature-focused programme to continue in the Argentine capital.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and two alternatives for the island excursion

The most substantial wildlife-watching section in this three-country selection is in the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The journey goes via Quito and Baltra Airport to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), where the programme includes the island highlands, giant tortoises and lava tunnels.

The following day is dedicated to a boat excursion. The programme includes **one of two routes**, not both at once:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach: an island excursion with opportunities to observe seabirds in their natural habitat.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrion: a walk near colonies of sea lions, iguanas and seabirds, followed by snorkelling near the cape; sightings of particular species are not guaranteed.

The specific option is confirmed after booking. Wildlife sightings depend on local conditions, and photographs in a guidebook are not a promise that the same species will appear on the day. For visitors primarily interested in birdwatching, the choice of island may matter more than the number of countries in the wider itinerary.

The archipelago is known for giant tortoises, iguanas and a variety of seabirds, but those facts describe **Galapagos wildlife in general**. They cannot be presented as a list of guaranteed sightings on this particular programme.

## Colombia: beautiful scenery without a dedicated safari

The Colombian stage begins in Medellín, followed by a day near [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/): mountains, the reservoir, scenic viewpoints and time exploring the town. This natural setting differs greatly from the ocean ecosystem of the Galapagos.

However, this is **an eight-hour sightseeing excursion**, not a specialist bird- or mammal-watching programme. The itinerary then visits Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. These destinations are primarily of cultural and historical interest; calling them safaris simply because Colombia is rich in biodiversity would be misleading.

| Country | Nature-related part of the tour |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu Falls and forest |
| Ecuador | Galapagos, Santa Cruz and one island route |
| Colombia | Guatapé and views across the reservoir |

## What to plan for wildlife watching

A standard ticket for a mainland flight is not sufficient for the Galapagos: the TCT transit control card, biosecurity baggage inspection and conservation fee must be checked separately. The national park administration describes these procedures. Included services and the amounts payable are verified before departure according to the traveller's nationality and passenger status.

Ecuador also involves changes in altitude and temperature: [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) is in the Andes, while the Galapagos sit at sea level. Closed-toe comfortable shoes, sun protection, protection for cameras against spray and the ability to observe birds from a distance are useful. Whether binoculars, a specialist camera or a dedicated naturalist guide are provided needs to be checked against the programme; none is confirmed automatically.

Food and objects that breach biosecurity regulations must not be introduced to the islands' natural environment. Weather and sea conditions can also affect the vessel's route. Ada Tours helps match guests' desired wildlife experiences with the actual excursions and allows time for flights and connections, but cannot control animal behaviour.

## When to choose another combination

If your main aim is to spend more time in the Galapagos, compare the extended tour with the [12-day Ecuador and Colombia programme](/multi-country/tour/ecuador-colombia-galapagos-12-days/). That shorter journey is not part of this selection because it does not include Argentina. If you want both waterfalls and the Galapagos in one long journey, the original [32-day programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) offers both, but requires time for the other six countries.

Other itineraries combining these three countries can be found in the [Argentina + Colombia + Ecuador catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador/), while the broader theme is covered by [multi-country Wildlife and Safari tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a visit to North Seymour guaranteed in the Galapagos?

No. The boat excursion follows one of two options: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrion. The selection is confirmed when booking.

### Is wildlife watching planned in Colombia?

The selected tour does not include a dedicated wildlife-watching excursion in Colombia. Its nature-related stop is the Guatapé area, while the remaining visits are predominantly urban.

### Will we see giant tortoises?

The Santa Cruz programme specifies an excursion to the highlands with giant tortoises. It is a substantive nature experience, but animal behaviour and viewing conditions depend on the situation on the day.

### Can the journey be shortened to these three countries?

The ready-made itinerary covers eight countries. An option visiting only Argentina, Ecuador and Colombia would require separate arrangements, new flights and confirmation that the relevant excursions are available.

## Four different experiences within one extensive journey

In this itinerary, [Argentina](/argentina/) brings Iguazu, Buenos Aires and tango; [Peru](/peru/) offers Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu; [Ecuador](/ecuador/) features Quito and the Galapagos; and [Colombia](/colombia/) introduces Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. It is a rewarding combination for travellers interested in [culture and history](/interests/culture-and-history/) as well as [nature and wildlife](/interests/wildlife/).

However, the current [ready-made 32-day tour of eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers far more than these four destinations. Between Buenos Aires and Puno in Peru, the itinerary includes a ferry excursion to Uruguay, Santiago, the Atacama Desert, Bolivian lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz. This selection must therefore be read as **an intersection of four countries within a longer journey**, not a ready-made 'Argentina–Peru–Ecuador–Colombia' route without intermediate stops.

The experiences follow a natural progression: large cities in the Southern Cone, high-altitude archaeological centres, island ecosystems and then a rich urban programme in Colombia. If you need a shorter journey visiting only these four countries, the route and price must be recalculated.

## Argentina: the big city and waterfalls before the Andes

In Argentina, the group explores Iguazu Falls from the Puerto Iguazú side and then arrives in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Here, a city tour covers La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta and other neighbourhoods, followed by a tango performance with dinner in the evening.

After Argentina, travellers take a day trip by ferry to Montevideo, return to Buenos Aires and fly to Santiago. This matters for travel documents: there is a second entry into Argentina, even though Uruguay is not mentioned in the title of this particular four-country selection.

The transition to the mountains is not immediate. After Santiago, travellers fly to Calama, transfer to the Atacama, continue through Bolivia and only then arrive in Peru. The high-altitude Bolivian section reaches above 4,000 metres. Anyone sensitive to altitude should assess not only Cusco in Peru but also the entire preceding stretch.

## Peru: Titicaca, archaeological monuments and a day at Machu Picchu

The Peruvian stage starts in the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) after the overland border crossing from Bolivia. The programme includes a visit to the Uros islands. A tourist bus then takes the group to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), stopping at historic sites along the way.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) has a full day devoted to it. According to the itinerary, the group visits with an English-speaking guide, lunch is included and the return to Cusco is by train. The following day, travellers visit Cusco's monuments before flying to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), where a sightseeing tour runs from Miraflores to the historic centre.

This is one of the most concentrated cultural sections of the 32-day journey. Travelling through Puno and Cusco means dealing with altitude, while visiting Machu Picchu involves rail transport and timed admission. Agree on a manageable pace in advance and check site-entry rules for the actual visiting date. Cutting this section to fit in another city elsewhere would change a substantial cultural component of the trip.

## Ecuador: where archaeology gives way to ocean wildlife

After Lima, travellers reach Quito, visit the equator-line area and fly the following day to the Galapagos Islands via Baltra. On Santa Cruz, the itinerary covers the highlands and Puerto Ayora, followed by a separate day of marine excursions.

There is one important limitation concerning the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/): **not all of the listed islands are promised on the same trip**. The basic tour includes one of two alternatives: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrion. The option is confirmed at booking. That is why specific bird species, marine animals or viewing sites cannot all be guaranteed by the broad label 'Galapagos'.

Before flying to the archipelago, travellers complete the separate TCT transit control procedure and a biosecurity baggage inspection. These formalities affect the time needed at the airport. The Ecuadorian stage includes a domestic flight, island transfers, a day at sea and a return via Guayaquil. It would be inaccurate to compare this with a single sightseeing day in Quito.

In terms of the experience, Ecuador's nature follows Peru's cultural heritage. This contrast is precisely what makes the combination attractive: Cusco and Machu Picchu are dominated by human-made sites, while the Galapagos are defined by natural ecosystems and the conditions for observing them.

## Colombia: from Medellín and Guatapé to the Caribbean coast and Bogotá

The programme includes a flight from Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The group then visits El Peñol and Guatapé, explores Comuna 13 and flies to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The following day is devoted to Cartagena's historic centre and fortifications.

After Cartagena, travellers arrive in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), with visits to museums and Monserrate. A separate excursion takes them to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá. The Colombian finale differs from Peru: attention turns to colonial and contemporary urban culture, architecture, local history and varied landscapes, from the Caribbean shoreline to the Andes.

The climate changes quickly too. Cartagena is on the warm Caribbean coast, while Bogotá is at altitude and substantially cooler. Light clothes for the coast need to be combined with a warm layer for the capital; after the mountains of Peru and Quito, travellers may need to reorganise their luggage once again.

## What to compare when history or nature is your main priority

| Interest | Where it features |
|---|---|
| Urban culture | Buenos Aires, Cartagena, Bogotá |
| Inca heritage | Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| High-altitude landscapes | Titicaca and the preceding Bolivian section |
| Island nature | Galapagos |
| Contemporary urban stories | Medellín, Comuna 13 |

Within this combination, Peru and Ecuador call for the most careful preparation regarding access to specific natural and historic sites. Colombia adds several different cities and domestic flights. Argentina sets the opening cultural scene, but the itinerary travels through other countries for quite some time before reaching Peru.

## Documents, payments and the true cost in travel time

The complete passport and visa itinerary covers Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Overland crossings, re-entry into Argentina, airport transfers and each country's requirements for the traveller's nationality must all be checked separately. Permission to enter one country does not automatically apply to its neighbour.

[Peru](/peru/) uses the sol, [Ecuador](/ecuador/) uses the US dollar, while Argentina and Colombia have their respective national pesos. Travellers should not assume that one bank card or a supply of US-dollar cash will solve every payment issue. We help review possible payments and backup methods in advance, but travellers need to confirm what actually works with their own banks and applicable restrictions.

The published programme includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers, excursions and admission tickets as specified in the itinerary. International flights and additional activities are expenses outside the tour price. When deciding, compare not only the starting price but also the trip's full duration, high-altitude exertion, number of hotel changes, the marine section in the Galapagos and personal spending.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia

### Is this a ready-made tour of exactly four countries?

No. The current selection includes a 32-day tour through eight countries. Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia lie between Argentina and Peru, and the programme begins in Brazil. A shortened four-country version must be arranged separately.

### Are both Machu Picchu and the Galapagos included?

Yes. A full day is reserved for Machu Picchu from Cusco, and the Galapagos section includes arrival on Santa Cruz and a separate island excursion. The exact marine-day route is chosen from two alternatives at booking.

### Where is altitude most demanding on this journey?

Pay particular attention to the high-altitude route through Bolivia and Peru and the Quito area. In Bolivia, the programme crosses areas above 4,000 metres. Altitude tolerance and access to medical care should be assessed before confirming flights and excursions.

### How many Colombian cities does the programme actually visit?

The itinerary includes Medellín with a trip to Guatapé, Cartagena and Bogotá with an excursion to Zipaquirá. Flights connect the main cities; Colombia is not reduced to a single transit day.

### Which excursions may change?

In the Galapagos, the programme already provides two alternative island routes, one of which is included. All other excursions follow the conditions, order and permitted changes in the full itinerary; the exact services should be checked against the [tour description](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).
